title: Fixed window, sliding window and leaky bucket

kcs.statement: A fixed-window counter allows N requests per clock-aligned window; it is cheap but can let up to 2N requests through in a short span around a window boundary.

A sliding-window log stores every request timestamp and counts those in the last window, which is exact but uses memory proportional to the request rate; a sliding-window counter approximates it by weighting the previous window's count.

A leaky bucket queues requests and processes them at a constant rate, turning bursts into a steady outflow and dropping requests when the queue is full, unlike a token bucket, which lets bursts through.

problem_ideas: Limit 100/min with a fixed window: 100 requests at 0:59 and 100 at 1:01; how many pass, and why is that a problem?
Sliding-window counter: the previous minute had 80, the current has 30, we are 25% into the window, the limit is 100; is the next request allowed?
Memory for a sliding-window log at 1,000 req/min per user with 8-byte timestamps for 1 million users
Pick an algorithm for calling a payment provider that must receive at most 10 calls/s, evenly spaced
Pick an algorithm for a public API that tolerates short bursts
Rank the four algorithms by memory per client and by accuracy
